'''Susan Nicole Houde-Walter''' (born 20 August 1954) is both an academic and executive with technical background in optical physics and engineering. Her specialties include laser physics, optoelectronics, optical materials, and imaging science, with applications in national security. She has traveled extensively with the United States military and served on science and policy boards, including the Army Science Board,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=The Army Science Board: Championing Innovation for 70 Years |url=https://asb.army.mil/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213022253/https://asb.army.mil/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 13, 2018 |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=asb.army.mil |language=en-US}}</ref> the Department of the Air Force Scientific Advisory Board,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Department of the Air Force Scientific Advisory Board |url=https://www.scientificadvisoryboard.af.mil/ |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.scientificadvisoryboard.af.mil}}</ref> the Intelligence Science and Technology Expert Group | National Academies,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Intelligence Science and Technology Experts Group |url=https://www.nationalacademies.org/our-work/intelligence-science-and-technology-experts-group |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.nationalacademies.org}}</ref> and the National Defense Industry Association board on Special Operations/Low Intensity Conflict.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Special Operations/Low Intensity Conflict |url=https://www.ndia.org/divisions/solic |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.ndia.org |language=en}}</ref>

Dr. Houde-Walter was elected to the Board of Directors and later to the presidential chain of Optica<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/default.htm |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref> (formerly, OSA), serving as its president in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |title=Past OSA Presidents |url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/leadership_and_volunteers/past_presidents/ |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> The Pentagon selected her for the 71st Joint Civilian Orientation Conference (JCOC),<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=JCOC: Joint Civilian Orientation Conference |url=https://www.war.gov/jcoc |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=U.S. Department of Defense |language=en-US}}</ref> held in the [[United States Central Command]]. She was awarded the Keeper of the Flame award in 2018<ref>{{Cite web |last=Amigone |first=Jackie |date=2018-12-20 |title=Two Leaders in Optics Win "Keeper of the Flame" Awards from National Women's Hall of Fame - Luminate % |url=https://luminate.org/two-leaders-in-optics-win-keeper-of-the-flame-awards-from-national-womens-hall-of-fame/ |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=Luminate |language=en-US}}</ref> by the [[National Women's Hall of Fame]].

== Early life and education ==
Houde-Walter was born as Susan Nicole Houde on 20 August 1954 in New York City, to Millicent (née Svoboda), a homemaker, and Raymond Houde, M.D.,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/39597081_Raymond_W_Houde |title=Raymond W. Houde's research while affiliated with Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center and other places |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> a pioneer in the management of chronic pain at the [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center|Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center]]. Susan was raised as graphic artist, and graduated from [[Sarah Lawrence College]] with a B.A. in liberal arts in 1976. She subsequently studied undergraduate physics at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]], [[The Institute of Optics]] at the [[University of Rochester]], and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] on an un-matriculated basis while working in New York City and Cambridge, Massachusetts. She was admitted to the masters and doctoral programs in optics at the University of Rochester in New York and produced both a master's<ref>{{cite thesis |type=Masters |last=Houde-Walter |first=Susan |date=1983 |title=Field-Assisted Ion Exchange in Glass |publisher=University of Rochester}}</ref> and doctoral thesis<ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Houde-Walter |first=Susan |date=1987 |title=Gradient-Index Profile Control in Glass |publisher=University of Rochester}}</ref> in the area of gradient-index optics made by ion exchange in glass, thesis advisor [[Duncan T. Moore|Duncan T Moore]].

== Career history ==
Houde-Walter served as Professor of Optics at the [[University of Rochester]] from 1987-2005.<ref>{{cite book |last=Hall |first=Dennis G. |url=http://www2.optics.rochester.edu/~stroud/BookHTML/ChapVII_pdf/VII_58.pdf |title=A Jewel in the Crown 75th Anniversary Essays The Institute of Optics University or Rochester |date=2004 |editor-last=Stroud Jr. |editor-first=Carlos R. |pages=306–308 |chapter=Chapter 7: Photonics at the Institute of Optics |access-date=February 10, 2019}}</ref> She was the first female regular faculty member for the first 80 years of the [[Institute of Optics]]’ history. She left the University of Rochester at rank of Full Professor of Optics (tenured) in 2005 and was appointed adjunct faculty at the, [[University of Arizona College of Optical Sciences]] that same year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Susan Houde-Walter Faculty Affiliation |url=http://www.optics.arizona.edu/research/faculty/profile/susan-houde-walter |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> Houde-Walter was elected to the Board of Directors and subsequently to the presidential chain of [[The Optical Society|Optica]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Susan N. Houde-Walter Biography |url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/history/biographies/susan-n--houde-walter/ |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> (formerly Optical Society of America, OSA).

Houde-Walter and her husband Will co-founded LaserMax, Inc., a provider of laser optical equipment for civilian and law enforcement. Later, as CEO, she spun off LMD Power of Light, a manufacturer of advanced laser equipment including quantum cascade lasers for military and other government customers.<ref name="LMD">{{cite web |title=About |url=https://www.lmd-corp.com/about/ |access-date=3 October 2022 |website=LaserMaxDefense (LMD)}}</ref> Dr. Houde-Walter holds over twenty-five patents<ref>{{cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Susan Houde-Walter |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/susan-houde-walter |access-date=2019-02-10 |website=JUSTIA}}</ref> and has published widely in the fields of optoelectronics and optical materials. She served as the director and professor of the Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science at the [[Rochester Institute of Technology]]<ref name="RIT">{{cite web |title=College of Science - RIT |url=https://www.rit.edu/science/directory/shwcis-susan-houde-walter |access-date=1 September 2022 |website=www.rit.edu}}</ref> from 2022 to 2023.

Houde-Walter held and currently holds positions on numerous science and policy boards for the United States Military and has traveled extensively in support. She was selected for the 71st [[Joint Civilian Orientation Conference]]<ref name=":4" /> in 2006, held in [[United States Central Command]]. She served on the [[Department of the Air Force Scientific Advisory Board]],<ref name=":1" /> and multiple terms on the [[Army Science Board]]<ref name=":0" /> and [[Intelligence Science and Technology Experts Group]].<ref name=":2" /> Houde-Walter also serves on the NDIA board on [[Special Operations/Low Intensity Conflict Division Board]].<ref name=":3" />

== Awards and recognitions ==
Houde-Walter is Fellow of both [[The Optical Society|Optica]] (1996) and the [[American Ceramic Society]] (2000). She has been recognized for her service with the [[Public Service Commendation Medal]], [[United States Department of the Army]] (2014) and the Commander’s Award for Public Service, [[United States Department of the Air Force]] (2016). In 2017, Dr. Houde-Walter was named the New York Photonics Entrepreneur of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rbj.net/2017/09/21/four-honored-with-photonics-awards/ |title=Four honored with photonics awards |website=Rochester Business Journal |date=21 September 2017 |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> In 2018, the [[National Women's Hall of Fame|National Women’s Hall of Fame]] recognized Dr. Houde-Walter with the Keeper of the Flame Award.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.womenofthehall.org/event/2018-keepers-of-the-flame/ |title=2018 Keeper of the Flame |website=National Women's Hall of Fame |access-date=2019-02-10}}</ref> In 2020, Optica awarded Houde-Walter the Stephen D. Fantone Distinguished Service Award.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=OSA Distinguished Service Award|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/distinguishedservice/|access-date=|website=The Optical Society}}</ref>
